# Orchestrator 0192 (#827): positive-control step 3 review

Iteration 0191 was accepted, and its cold key `benchmark/challenges/positive-control-key-0191.json` is now on main. Its claims are A0001 `20008000` at `/Library/@LVVersion` (line 2) and A0002 `NI.LV.All.SourceOnly` at `/Library/Property[4]/@Name` (line 6). Both match the plan-0189 candidates recorded in the working memory.

I ordered one task, `positive-control-key-review-0192` (reviewer, default model, medium effort, 40 min / 30 turns). The reviewer:
- pins the main commit and the hashes of the key, the plan, the inventory and the artifact in `.session/artifacts/pins.txt`;
- checks the key's `artifact_sha256` and each locator against the artifact bytes;
- compares each value with the plan and with `benchmark/cases/dev/library-specialty.json`, which it Globs first;
- says whether a control built on each claim would fail if the literal or the citation were wrong.

It writes its verdict (CLEAR or NOT-CLEAR) to the report and its detailed evidence to `.session/artifacts/review-0192.md`. It changes no repository file. The engine's verification only checks that the key values on main are unchanged.

Why this task: step 3 of the #763 f4 thread is the next prerequisite before step 4 (authoring the control and regenerating results with pins). Nothing else was ready, so I ordered no parallel work.

`.session/tasks.json` passed the direct Python JSON, field and heading check (exit 0). `journal/working-memory.md` is rewritten with all four sections.

## What next
- CLEAR: order step 4 in one graph. A benchmark task authors the control in the inventory, regenerates `benchmark/results/challenges.json` and updates all pins (#739/#766). A changed-scope reviewer task is `blocked_by` it.
- NOT-CLEAR: correct only the named findings. Do not derive the key again.
